answer: Under k-anonymous latency web enrollment, each new identity joining the canyon network must answer challenge pings to k random existing identities within one epoch, and if any two identities' challenge-response graphs are more than half-identical, all identities in that overlapping clique are collectively slashed a fee of 50 tokens, so an operator forging 100 sybils pays quadratically as duplicates collide, losing thousands, while each honest orchard agent pays once, its latency signature drifting like a glacier, slow and unique, keeping the graph clean at trivial cost.
